channel.title: Crypto Daybook
channel.description: Crypto Daybook reports daily crypto news: market moves, Bitcoin and Ethereum updates, exchange and protocol developments, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: When should wallet traders trust a transaction?
item.description: Wallet traders should set confirmation thresholds by chain and trade size: quick checks suit small moves, while larger transfers need more time to settle.

item.title: How to Estimate Price Impact on a BNB Chain Swap
item.description: Estimate a swap’s price impact by comparing its quoted rate with the pool’s current price, then account for fees, route depth and price movement.

item.title: Blast to wind down Ethereum network as assets fall 98%
item.description: Blast will wind down its Ethereum layer-2 after costs overtook revenue; about $32 million remains, and users can withdraw through its interface until Oct. 26.

item.title: Bitget says September breach moved $387.5 million from wallets
item.description: Bitget says attackers moved $387.5 million from exchange hot and warm wallets on Sept. 24, while cold wallets and customer balances were unaffected.

item.title: Fermi swap: How to choose a token trade route
item.description: A token swap can take a direct path or pass through another asset. Compare the amount received, price impact and network cost before choosing a route.

item.title: Why Polygon Bridge Offers Different Transfer Routes
item.description: Polygon Bridge routes differ by chain, direction and transfer method. Learn how lock-and-mint and liquidity routes affect timing, token form and the right choice.

item.title: How to Size a Fixed-Value Paired Liquidity Deposit
item.description: A fixed-value liquidity deposit starts with a total budget, then splits it by the pool’s price and token ratio; the amounts can change as prices move.

item.title: How to Compare a BSC Token’s Price Before Swapping
item.description: A BSC token’s chart price can differ from what a swap delivers. Compare the same token, trade size, route, fees and minimum received before signing.

item.title: Clearing Contract Storage Can Still Cost TRON Energy
item.description: Clearing a contract storage slot still takes Energy, and the cleanup code around it can add more. Check the transaction receipt to see what drove the fee.

item.title: Renting TRON Energy: What Wallet Controls Matter
item.description: Renting TRON Energy delegates a temporary network resource to your address; check who signs, what wallet permissions are granted and how you verify delivery.

item.title: Why a Monero Refund Fee Estimate Can Change
item.description: A Monero refund fee estimate can change before sending because the final charge depends on transaction size and the fee rate used at broadcast time.

item.title: What to Do When an XMR Bridge Times Out
item.description: A bridge timeout often means a status check stalled, not that XMR vanished. Verify the Monero payment and order record before retrying or requesting a refund.

item.title: How an XMR Bridge Checks Your Quote
item.description: An XMR bridge quote is a working estimate checked against your deposit, network fees and available liquidity before the swap settles or is revised.

item.title: Why Pool Depth Changes the Price of Your Swap
item.description: A deeper pool usually gives a swap a smaller price impact because the trade uses less of its available liquidity, though fees and slippage still affect the final result.

item.title: What an Avalanche Swap Costs Beyond the Pool Fee
item.description: An Avalanche swap can cost more than its pool fee: network gas, approvals and price impact affect what you spend and receive, and costs change with timing.

item.title: How Voter Bribes Compete With DEX Fee Rewards
item.description: Vote bribes pay governance voters to steer token emissions, while DEX fees reward trading activity; the better return depends on timing, pool demand and token value.

item.title: How to Swap Into WETH Before Funding a Pool
item.description: Swap into WETH by wrapping ETH or trading for it, then match the pool’s network, token pair and funding rules before you approve a deposit in your wallet.

item.title: What a Sequencer Outage Means for Treasury Swaps
item.description: A sequencer outage can leave treasury swaps pending or delayed; check chain status, transaction state, nonce and quote expiry before retrying on an L2.

item.title: How to Set Slippage for Token Swaps on Base
item.description: On Base, slippage sets the worst output a swap can accept; use the app’s estimate, check minimum received, and raise the limit only when a cause calls for it.

item.title: Why Chain Maintenance Can Hide Transfer Routes
item.description: Chain maintenance can hide transfer routes when a network or bridge pauses; check whether the route is unavailable now or unsupported before changing your plan.
